beats.text: Wonderful. Hold that feeling while I finish the parking story.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're waiting on a video call for us to toast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me on first. They need the parking story, or my face will look like a comment on your promotion.

records.mechanism: A makes understanding A's mood a prerequisite for celebrating B's achievement, extending that requirement to the waiting audience.
records.confusableConcept: Simple attention-seeking would merely demand a turn; A treats explaining personal unhappiness as necessary to the proper reception of B's promotion.
records.distinguishingEvidence: A3 asks B to hold excitement while A explains the afternoon; A5 says the waiting callers must understand A's face before they can toast B.
records.alternativeComparison: The promotion version expands a demand for attention to a remote gathering under the guise of protecting B's celebration; the birthday version controls the intensity of celebration already underway.
records.reason: The supplied candidate review identified repeated postponement and limited new pressure. Preserved A1 through A3 and added a waiting video-call toast. Preserved firstPass exactly. Separate internal coach-1.0 reread: fidelity 5 (A5 makes A's visible mood everyone's interpretive priority), logic 5 (A3 acknowledges B2's promotion; B4's callers cause A5's request to address them first), relationship 4 (B4 has people waiting for a shared toast), heightening 4 (A5 commandeers a larger audience), specificity 4 (A3 parking story and B4 video call), brevityWit 4 (A5 treats A's expression as a threat to the promotion's reception). Total 90; five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words, and all dialogue gates pass. This is internal model review only.
records.reservation: The content of the parking upset remains unspecified. A5 must sincerely believe the callers need emotional context, or the scene reduces to knowingly stealing the spotlight.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 openly conditions leadership on slow speech, and A3 admits the calm face is not ready; dependence is scarcely quiet.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 repeats B2's missing delivery; A5 counts B4's invoice as a second loss.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 supply bad facts but show little independent need or emotional pressure.

heightening.evidence: A5 extends the slowing tactic to one loss per breath without changing the underlying dependency.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a chaired meeting, with a delivery and invoice specifying the business problem.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'One loss per breath' follows the accumulating losses and attempted professional control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll chair the delivery meeting. We're in control. Keep your voice just there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The van's missing. I'm trying not to panic.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Keep trying. We'll establish its last location.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll fetch the driver. He's shouting in the corridor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Brief him outside first. Then sit beside me and give the report in your voice.

records.mechanism: A projects procedural control while discreetly requiring B to regulate the emotional conditions that sustain it.
records.confusableConcept: Open anxiety management would foreground A's distress; this card maintains the leadership claim while outsourcing calm.
records.distinguishingEvidence: Revised A1 claims control, A3 redirects B's effort not to panic, and A5 needs B's calm voice between A and the shouting driver.
records.alternativeComparison: The meeting version uses a colleague as an emotional intermediary; the wedding version recruits a practical helper while protecting A's visible steadiness.
records.reason: Replaced the explicit calm-face admission with procedural dependence; retained delivery-meeting context. Internal coach-1.0 reread: fidelity 4 (A1 asserts control; A5 quietly relies on B), logic 5 (A3 uses B2's panic and van; A5 uses B4's shouting driver), relationship 4 (B has an operational task), heightening 4 (A5 requires continued proximity), specificity 5 (meeting and corridor), brevityWit 4 (A5 borrows B's voice). Total 86; applicable gates pass.
records.reservation: Asking for calm reports can resemble competent management; A's insistence on B sitting beside them supplies the vulnerable dependence.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims composure and A3 controls alarming language, but A5 makes the vulnerability quite overt.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 reframes B2's leaning cake; A5 requests delayed reporting of B4's fall.

relationship.evidence: B2 reports a problem and B4 escalates its urgency, exposing the inadequacy of A's euphemism.

heightening.evidence: A5 moves from controlling vocabulary to postponing acknowledgment until physically prepared.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes the wedding; B2 and B4 give an immediate, worsening cake problem.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's requested past tense precisely connects linguistic control with the falling cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The wedding's under control. Tell me about the cake in that lovely calm voice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's leaning. I can hold the stand level.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. A minor adjustment. Keep talking like that while you hold it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you'll have to help. My hands are shaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. We'll steady it together. You count us in; your voice hasn't started shaking.

records.mechanism: A sustains a public claim of control by depending on B's remaining calm even while joining the practical rescue.
records.confusableConcept: Denying bad news would only rename or delay it; A can act provided B supplies enough composure.
records.distinguishingEvidence: Revised A3 needs B to keep speaking calmly, and A5 joins the rescue while relying on B's unshaken voice.
records.alternativeComparison: The wedding version makes mutual assistance expose the dependency; the meeting version filters another person's agitation through a calmer colleague.
records.reason: The original narrowly missed acceptance and leaned toward euphemistic avoidance. Internal coach-1.0 reread: fidelity 5 (A1 control claim; A5 borrowed calm), logic 5 (A3 uses B2's stand; A5 uses B4's shaking hands), relationship 4 (B requires help), heightening 4 (A must act while preserving dependence), specificity 5 (unstable wedding cake), brevityWit 4 (A5 distinguishes voice from hands). Total 92; applicable gates pass.
records.reservation: The revised ending is less verbally sharp than the past-tense joke, but more clearly makes another person's composure necessary to A.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 diagnoses resentment and A3 corrects B's account, but A5 never prescribes the proper response.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 recasts B2's tidiness as protection; A5 treats B4's objection as diagnostic success.

relationship.evidence: B4 clearly wants the analysis stopped, but A5 provides another label without changing the interaction.

heightening.evidence: A5 congratulates the process rather than moving from interpretation to an imposed response.

specificity.evidence: A1's folded napkin supplies a visible, playable reaction to misinterpret.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'Order as emotional protection' efficiently converts a mundane correction into supposed confirmation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said dinner was fine while folding your napkin. That's guarded resentment.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It means the napkin was untidy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're restoring order because you feel unheard. Tell me what you needed from dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: To eat without being analysed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good boundary. Now say it without hiding behind the napkin, so I can acknowledge it properly.

records.mechanism: A treats B's reactions as expert-readable evidence, overrides B's explanation and prescribes how B should express the diagnosed feeling.
records.confusableConcept: Merely naming emotions would stop at diagnosis; the exact card also corrects interpretation and dictates a proper response.
records.distinguishingEvidence: Revised A3 replaces B2's tidiness explanation, and A5 turns B4's request to stop into a coached boundary performance.
records.alternativeComparison: This version absorbs direct resistance into a prescribed expression of boundaries; the biscuit version diagnoses a practical request and imposes an emotional prerequisite.
records.reason: Added prescription while retaining the dinner and napkin. Internal coach-1.0 reread: fidelity 5 (A3 diagnoses and prescribes), logic 5 (A3 uses B2's order; A5 uses B4's boundary), relationship 4 (B wants an ordinary meal), heightening 4 (A5 regulates resistance itself), specificity 5 (dinner and napkin), brevityWit 4 (A5 approves the boundary while violating it). Total 92; applicable spoken-dialogue gates pass.
records.reservation: A's instructions are fictional dialogue to B, not coaching for the real partner; delivery should express sincere expertise rather than deliberate bullying.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 interpret laughter, and A5 diagnoses comfort-seeking, but no clear proper response is prescribed.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 disputes B2's account of humor; A5 directly interprets B4's biscuit request.

relationship.evidence: B4 tries moving to a practical request, but B's desired ordinary interaction stays lightly developed.

heightening.evidence: A5 applies the same labeling tactic to biscuits without increasing the consequences of A's expertise.

specificity.evidence: A1's laugh and B4's biscuits suggest a social gathering with playable objects.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'Which feeling would you like with them?' reads more like a menu joke than a sincere prescription.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're laughing very quickly at Dad's impression. Nervous about meeting my parents?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: No, the impression was funny.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's approval-seeking. You can let a joke pass without earning your place.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you pass the biscuits? I missed lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Comfort-seeking now. Say 'I belong here' before you take one. Let's feed the insecurity first.

records.mechanism: A converts laughter and hunger into expert emotional diagnoses, then prescribes reassurance instead of accepting B's stated explanations.
records.confusableConcept: Ordinary supportive reassurance would respond to an expressed concern; A asserts hidden feelings despite B's corrections.
records.distinguishingEvidence: A3 overrides B2's explanation of amusement with approval-seeking; A5 recasts B4's missed lunch as insecurity requiring an affirmation before eating.
records.alternativeComparison: The family visit version imposes reassurance on a guest seeking food; the napkin version converts a direct demand to stop analysis into further analysis.
records.reason: The rejected candidate confused ownership of the joke and padded its final prescription. Kept the introduced family visit, made Dad's impression consistent across A1 and B2, and shortened A5 to a specific affirmation before the biscuit. Preserved firstPass exactly. Separate internal coach-1.0 reread: fidelity 5 (A3 and A5 diagnose, correct and prescribe), logic 5 (A3 reinterprets B2's amusement; A5 responds to B4's hunger and biscuits), relationship 4 (B wants amusement and food accepted literally), heightening 4 (A5 makes emotional compliance precede eating), specificity 5 (A1 meeting parents and B4 missed lunch), brevityWit 4 (A5 feeding insecurity follows the biscuit request). Total 92; five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words, and all dialogue gates pass. Prescriptions are fictional speech to B. This is internal model review only.
records.reservation: A5's feeding metaphor remains polished, though it now directly expresses A's priority. A's behavior needs sincere confidence in helping B rather than conscious obstruction of hospitality.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims meeting access through three winters of work; A3 makes cracked hands an investment credential.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's investor restriction; A5 supplies dates in response to B4's contribution-record requirement.

relationship.evidence: B2 controls admission and B4 supplies a documentary route, materially changing A's argument.

heightening.evidence: A5 commits to entering endured hardship into the formal contribution record.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a shop and meeting; A3's cracked hands concretize the claimed sacrifice.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'Start with the winters' translates endurance into the requested documentation economically.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I worked through three winters to open this shop. Leave me a chair at the meeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only investors are invited.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My cracked hands invested before the cheque books arrived.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The form only accepts money. Could you speak under an investor's name?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three winters in an unheated shop, and I need a sponsor? Put frostbite under capital. I'm speaking under my own name.

records.mechanism: A treats endured physical hardship as a credential for access and an independent voice in the shop's decisions.
records.confusableConcept: A generic contribution claim could rely on output or money; A specifically argues from the personal cost of the work.
records.distinguishingEvidence: A3 sets cracked hands against B2's investor requirement; A5 answers B4's proxy offer by demanding that endured cold qualify A to speak under A's own name.
records.alternativeComparison: The shop version rejects borrowed institutional standing and demands recognition of hardship as capital; the audition version challenges relocation that would deprive A of an attentive audience.
records.reason: The supplied candidate review found the final documentation offer insufficiently developed. Preserved A1 through A3, clarified the form's monetary restriction and added B4's offer of a proxy identity. Preserved firstPass exactly. Separate internal coach-1.0 reread: fidelity 5 (A3 and A5 claim standing through bodily hardship), logic 5 (A3 answers B2's investors; A5 addresses B4's form and sponsor), relationship 4 (B4 offers access while withholding independent recognition), heightening 4 (A5 demands both reclassification and a voice under A's own name), specificity 5 (A1 shop meeting and A5 unheated winters), brevityWit 4 (A5 enters frostbite as capital). Total 92; five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words, and all dialogue gates pass. This is internal model review only.
records.reservation: The form and sponsor route are illustrative comic procedure, not a claim about real governance. A's grievance can be reasonable; the heightened behavior lies in demanding that physical suffering count as capital.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 invokes six months of waiting as entitlement; A5 uses shared endurance to demand patience.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 accommodates B2's verse limit through duration; A5 turns B4's 'Everyone waited' into expected understanding.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants a limited audition and B4 invokes fairness to other people waiting.

heightening.evidence: A5 concentrates the claimed entitlement into refusing to rush the verse's last note.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes an audition after six months; B2 defines the requested performance length.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'Good' reverses B4's fairness objection into support for the prolonged note.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I slept outside this theatre for two nights. Please let me finish my audition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A verse is enough. We need the room for the next applicant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two nights on those steps earned me one chorus indoors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can finish in the corridor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then bring the panel. I didn't sleep outside to have my big moment overheard through a door.

records.mechanism: A treats physical hardship endured while waiting as proof of deserving additional audition time and the panel's continued attention.
records.confusableConcept: Simple ambition would argue from talent or the importance of the song; A repeatedly bases the demand on sleeping outside.
records.distinguishingEvidence: A3 converts two nights on the steps into an earned chorus; A5 invokes the same hardship to require the panel to accompany B4's proposed relocation.
records.alternativeComparison: The audition version accepts a different location only if the audience follows, expanding a demand for time into one for attention; the shop version seeks independent institutional standing by redefining capital.
records.reason: The supplied candidate review identified modest heightening and an unclear appeal to the panel's shared waiting. Kept the audition setting, replaced the abstract six-month wait with two nights on the theatre steps, and gave B a room-scheduling need plus a corridor compromise. Preserved firstPass exactly. Separate internal coach-1.0 reread: fidelity 5 (A3 and A5 explicitly derive entitlement from endured hardship), logic 5 (A3 answers B2's verse limit; B4's corridor causes A5's demand to bring the panel), relationship 4 (B2 must accommodate the next applicant and B4 offers another space), heightening 4 (A5 now claims the panel's movement and attention), specificity 5 (A1 theatre steps and B4 corridor), brevityWit 4 (A5 makes the practical compromise require moving the audience). Total 92; five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words, and all dialogue gates pass. This is internal model review only.
records.reservation: Sleeping outside establishes a stronger hardship than the original wait. B4's corridor offer can sound dismissive, but it remains a playable attempt to free the audition room without entirely silencing A.
